region.text: the territory of the Turkestan Krai (RT), Tashkent the capital

ledger.note: 1918: the Turkestan Soviet Federative Republic is proclaimed at Tashkent. 'The Turkestan Soviet Federative Republic was officially proclaimed on 30 April 1918'; constitution 15 October 1918. The region is the researcher's reading: the TA page names no oblast.

1918: the Ashkhabad rising takes Transcaspia. 'On 14 July 1918 The Ashkhabad Executive Committee was founded ... following their successful revolt against the Bolsheviks of Tashkent'; infobox 'Established: 12 July 1918'; based at Ashgabat, Transcaspian Oblast.

the countryside surrounding Tashkent

region.text: Ferghana and the countryside surrounding Tashkent

ledger.note: 1918: Basmachi bands hold the Fergana valley and the Tashkent countryside. By the end of the year 'decentralized bands of fighters, totaling roughly 20,000, controlled Ferghana and the countryside surrounding Tashkent'. A rebel overlay on the nominal extent, not a change of sovereignty.

1920: the Tashkent countryside returns to the republic. No page dates it; bridged from Madamin Bey's defection to the Soviet side in March (after the winter of 1919-20) and the Red Army's arrival in September 1919.

1920: the Tashkent Soviet regains Transcaspia. 'By 1920 the Tashkent Soviet had regained control of the area'; infobox 'Disestablished: February 1920' (the lead says July 1919). The month is the infobox's.

1920: the republic becomes the Turkestan Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic. 'On 24 September 1920 it became the Turkestan Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic'; from 30 December 1922 it is listed within the RSFSR and the Soviet Union.
1924: the last Basmachi presence in Fergana ends. A Ferghana presence under Korshirmat lasted 'until 1924'.

wars.name: Transcaspian campaign (Malleson mission)
wars.outcome: The Ashkhabad government, helped by the Anglo-Indian Malleson mission, held Transcaspia until the British withdrew; by 1920 the Tashkent Soviet had regained it.
wars.note: Dates: TG's lead says 1918 to July 1919, its infobox February 1920.

wars.outcome: Armed resistance that began in the summer of 1918 around Kokand (Ergash) and lasted into the 1920s; no border change while the republic lasted.
wars.note: 'fought Bolshevik forces until the 1920s as part of the conservative Basmachi rebellion' (TA). BP: it took the Red Army until 1934 to suppress it.

certainty.note: A civil-war state: control 'limited to only a few railway junctions' in 1918 (TA) and contested by the Basmachi; the 1920 enclaves of Bukhara and Khiva are drawn at the old protectorate lines.

notes:
Written for batch ia-03-x from five pages (TA, TG, SO, RT, DEL). No Cliopatria row; the land lies inside Cliopatria's Russian Republic 1917-1919 and Republics of the Soviet Union 1920-1921 shapes.
Unsettled: the TA page gives no oblast list and no area, so the extent is Russian Turkestan's (a reading); Semirechye's real control (White and Cossack forces held the north until 1919-20) and the Fergana front are on no page opened. TG's own dates disagree (lead July 1919, infobox February 1920).
Successors: the Uzbek SSR, Turkmen SSR, Tajik ASSR, Kara-Kirghiz AO and Karakalpak AO of 1924 have no dossiers (and the 1924-1991 union republics may not need any); all are recorded under the union dossier slug. Counterparts needing dossiers: transcaspian-provisional-government and basmachi-movement (both written in this batch).
